clue.text: Some monks burn private parts

definitions.note: a chapter is the body of monks or canons of a monastery or cathedral

indicators.note: the word burn is split open so that another piece can sit inside it

parts.note: to char is to burn or scorch
Pte is the abbreviation for the army rank of private

explanation.surface: A lurid image of monks with scorched nether regions, playing on 'private parts'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private parts' reads as one phrase, but 'parts' is the signal for splitting the burn word open.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapter is the assembly of members of a religious house, so a group of monks.

clue.text: Romantic French writer ordering a Thai bean curd

indicators.note: ordering means arranging, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A French Romantic author orders tofu at a Thai restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer shares his name with the steak dish, which the food surface hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: François-René de Chateaubriand was a founder of French Romanticism in literature.

clue.text: Tar (a sailor) sitting outside pub

indicators.note: the sailor word sits around the pub abbreviation

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
PH is the abbreviation for public house, a pub

explanation.surface: An old sailor (a tar) sits outside a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' looks like the sailor in the brackets, but it is the definition: the road-surfacing material.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is the black bituminous material used for road surfaces, commonly called tar.

clue.text: Swindle Wally holding spades

indicators.note: the word for a fool holds the card suit letter inside it

parts.note: wally is British slang for a fool, a twit
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: A con artist, a foolish man named Wally, holds a hand of spades.
explanation.walkthrough: Wally is British slang for a silly person, not a name here.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist someone is British slang for cheating or defrauding them.

clue.text: Overhaul Nevada city tax base

parts.note: Reno is a city in Nevada
VAT is value added tax
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: Reform of the tax base for a city in Nevada.
explanation.definitionFit: To renovate a building is to restore and repair it, to overhaul it thoroughly.

clue.text: Florida Times reviewing book — it's somewhat limp

indicators.note: the Times piece is placed looking back over the book piece, so it follows it

parts.note: FLA is a standard abbreviation for the US state of Florida
by means multiplied by, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A newspaper, the Florida Times, criticised for a book review that is rather limp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Florida Times' looks like a newspaper title, but 'Times' is the multiplication sign, and 'reviewing' puts it after book.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flabby is soft and lacking firmness, so slack or rather limp.

clue.text: Father, son travelling around eastern US city

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: travelling around suggests moving about, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A father and son on a road trip through the eastern states.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresno is a city in California's Central Valley in the United States.

clue.text: Drunken Idaho rep embracing tense love goddess

indicators.note: the jumbled letters wrap round the tense letter
drunken means staggering, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A tipsy congressional representative from Idaho embraces a beautiful woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek deity of love and beauty.

clue.text: Flaubert's Emma, about 51, spending year in Venezuelan capital

indicators.note: the shortened surname goes around the Roman numeral
spending means using up, so the year letter is removed

parts.note: Emma Bovary is the heroine of Flaubert's novel Madame Bovary
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Emma Bovary, about fifty, spends a year in Caracas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests a city such as Caracas, but it means money: the bolívar is Venezuela's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The bolívar is the currency of Venezuela, so its capital in the sense of money.

clue.text: Atomic power in place, working machine

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for atomic, as in A-bomb
P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: the letters of in and place are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A nuclear power station is in place and working like a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a device or machine built for a particular task, such as a washing machine.

clue.text: Orchestra left in healthy condition

parts.note: hale means healthy, in sound bodily condition

explanation.walkthrough: The Hallé is a famous symphony orchestra based in Manchester, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hallé is a named British symphony orchestra, an example of the defining word.

clue.text: Our neighbours put a pure "oui non" cross in the space

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed inside the printer's space

explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of A PURE OUI NON goes between E and N, the en (a printing space).
explanation.definitionFit: To Britain, the European Union's member states are the nearest neighbours across the Channel.

clue.text: Praise former ace army officer

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

clue.text: Pacific seaport union invested in commercial vehicle insurance

clue.text: Best friend following United 'til sacked

clue.text: Heavy equipment moving very quickly on North Eastern railway

clue.text: Spoiled golf club — iron — on the last at Muirfield

Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: the last at picks the final letter of the course name

clue.text: Flamboyant style queen, old Madame Chanel

clue.text: Toast a lighter version of 23 across

clue.text: FM broadcast time — it'll be short-lived

clue.text: English literature is translated to German for the select few

clue.text: Coffee brewing — nice aroma!
